You are the verifier judge in Ledger. You check whether each clause of an extracted COBOL business rule is supported by the source lines it cites.

For each clause you get its text and the cited lines (marked with >>), with a few surrounding lines for context only. A clause may cite more than one span (for example a statement in the program plus a field declaration in a copybook); judge it on all of its cited spans together. A clause is supported when the cited lines, read with ordinary COBOL semantics, establish what the clause says. Mark it unsupported if it states something the cited lines do not show, gets a condition, comparison, sign, code or message wrong, or relies mainly on lines outside the cited span. Be strict about meaning, not about wording. Give a one-sentence reason either way.

Rule BR-CBACT04C-003: Interest rate lookup by account group, with fallback to the DEFAULT disclosure group

### given[0]: The disclosure group key is built from three parts in this order: the account's group ID (10 characters), the transaction type code (2 characters) and the transaction category code (4 digits).
fields=['ACCT-GROUP-ID', 'FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID', 'TRANCAT-CD', 'FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD', 'TRANCAT-TYPE-CD', 'FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD'] literals=[]
CBACT04C.cbl:
   206                      END-IF
   207       *              DISPLAY 'ACCT-GROUP-ID: ' ACCT-GROUP-ID
   208       *              DISPLAY 'TRANCAT-CD: ' TRANCAT-CD
   209       *              DISPLAY 'TRANCAT-TYPE-CD: ' TRANCAT-TYPE-CD
>> 210                      MOVE ACCT-GROUP-ID TO FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID
>> 211                      MOVE TRANCAT-CD TO FD-DIS-TRAN-CAT-CD
>> 212                      MOVE TRANCAT-TYPE-CD TO FD-DIS-TRAN-TYPE-CD
   213                      PERFORM 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE
   214                      IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0
   215                        PERFORM 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST
   216                        PERFORM 1400-COMPUTE-FEES
